answer: The jetty multiplier is published, charged in sonnet, and kernel lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 4367 identities would post 1696 proofs and burn roughly 20 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
